title: Why We Stand Behind Our Work — And What That Actually Means
content:
###  **Why We Do Not Promise Lead Counts** 

Any company that guarantees a specific number of leads is either guessing or building in enough margin that the guarantee costs them nothing. 

Homeowner timing, weather, seasonality, and how quickly a client follows up are all real variables that sit outside a field team's control. Promising a number that depends on them is not confidence — it is marketing. 

###  **What We Do Commit To** 

Every contracted hour worked and documented. Activity reviewed on an ongoing basis rather than summarized at the end. Representatives held to a standard, and replaced quickly when they do not meet it. 

And if a client feels the contracted field activity did not deliver what was agreed, we return to the territory and run an additional period at no charge. 

###  **Why We Can Offer That** 

The commitment is only sustainable because of how selective the hiring is. A company staffing for availability could not afford to make it — they would be redoing work constantly. 

When you know who is going into a territory, standing behind the work is a much easier promise to keep. 

###  **What It Is Not** 

It is a defined remedy, not an open-ended arrangement. It is requested in writing, runs for a set period, and is available once. That structure keeps it meaningful for a client and honest on our side.
